Part 1 of Block Diffusion RooflinesPrevious: SummaryNext: 2 · The linear part

What do we need to track?

In order for us to state our main result (Proposition 1), we need to define the key quantities which govern the inference throughput of AR and TD. These quantities determine whether moving bytes (weights and KV cache) or performing actual work (matrix multiplies) is the limiting factor, i.e., whether the model is memory-bound or compute-bound. In order to do so, we need to compute the FLOPs of a forward pass of an AR model and those of a TD model. Similarly, we need to compute how many bytes are moved during a forward pass of the AR and TD models. By doing so, we will be able to establish the arithmetic intensities of both models, i.e., to answer the question: "how many FLOPs are used for each byte that is moved by the model?".

We consider a batch of \(B\) sequences, each with \(C\) tokens in its KV cache. An AR step is one forward pass and advances each sequence by one token1. On the other hand, TD advances each sequence by a canvas of \(b\) tokens, in \(S\) denoising passes and one commit pass. This is block diffusion (Arriola et al., 2025) with a KV cache over committed canvases. Throughout the blogpost, our running example is DiffusionGemma 26B-A4B (DiffusionGemma technical report, 2026).

A denoising pass costs \(r\) times a forward pass2. Hence, a canvas costs \(\omega = Sr + 1\) forward passes, and TD commits \(\mathrm{TPF} = b/\omega\) tokens per forward pass.

Figure 5 · interactive

In the \(\omega = S + 1\) passes of one canvas, AR commits \(\omega\) tokens and TD commits \(b\).

Press Play or Step to run the passes one at a time; change the canvas length and the number of denoising passes.

Top row: the forward passes in time order, each of which reads the weights once; the last one is the commit pass. Blue: the tokens AR has committed, one per pass. Orange: TD's canvas of \(b\) positions, refined by each of the \(S\) denoising passes and committed by the last pass, all \(b\) at once. A dense model with \(r = 1\), so a canvas costs \(\omega = S + 1\) passes; the default is the running example, \(b = 256\) and \(S = 14\). The readout gives \(\mathrm{TPF} = b/\omega\), which is the roofline bound \(\Gamma\) when both passes are memory-bound.

Costs of a pass

A pass reads the weights and the KV cache from memory and spends FLOPs on both. Definition 1 gives the sizes these costs depend on, and Definition 2 combines them into the FLOPs \(F\) and bytes \(Q\) of an AR step and of a TD pass. Don't forget to click on a formula to get a reminder of the associated symbols!

Definition 1Coverage function and per-token costs

Coverage function

\(U_{n,k}(N) = n\bigl[1-(1-\tfrac{k}{n})^{N}\bigr]\)the coverage function: the expected number of distinct units touched by \(N\) independent, uniformly random selections of \(k\) units out of \(n\), and \(n\) when \(k \ge n\)

Linear layers

\(E,\ k\)experts per MoE layer and experts each token selects (128 and 8 for DiffusionGemma)
\(L\)layers, each with \(E\) experts (30)
\(W^e\)parameters of one expert in one layer (5.95M)
\(W_{\mathrm{ne}}\)non-expert parameters of all layers, without the vocabulary (1.66B)

Shapes and precision

\(\mathcal G,\ \mathcal W,\ \mathcal S\)sets of the global-attention, sliding-window and sparse layers (5, 25 and none)
\(n_q,\ n_{kv,\ell},\ h_\ell\)query heads, KV heads and head dimension of layer \(\ell\) (16 query heads; 2 KV heads of dimension 512 on the global layers, 8 of dimension 256 on the window layers)
\(g = n_q/n_{kv,\ell}\)query heads per KV head on the global layers (8)
\(w,\ m\)earlier tokens that a window layer sees (1,023), and cached tokens that each query selects in a sparse layer (2,048 in the sparse variant of Part 3)
\(n_{I,\ell},\ h_{I,\ell}\)heads and head dimension of the indexer of sparse layer \(\ell\) (8 and 128 in the sparse variant)
\(s_w,\ s_{kv},\ s_I\)bytes per weight (2 in BF16, 16-bit floats; 1 in FP8, 8-bit floats), per element of the KV cache (2) and per element of the indexer's keys (1)
\(\kappa^c\)K/V tensors that a layer caches per KV head and per token (2: keys and values stored separately; 1 for a global layer whose \(K = V\) is stored once)

Attention 3

\(\alpha_G = 4n_q\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}h_\ell\)attention FLOPs per query and per cached token, global layers
\(\alpha_W = 4n_q\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal W}h_\ell\)the same, sliding-window layers
\(\alpha_S = 4n_q\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal S}h_\ell\)the same, sparse layers, per selected token
\(\alpha_I = 2\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal S}n_{I,\ell}h_{I,\ell}\)the same, for the indexer, the scan that selects a sparse layer's tokens (Part 3)
\(\nu_G = s_{kv}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\kappa^cn_{kv,\ell}h_\ell\)KV bytes per cached token, global layers
\(\nu_W = s_{kv}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal W}\kappa^cn_{kv,\ell}h_\ell\)the same, sliding-window layers
\(\nu_S = s_{kv}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal S}\kappa^cn_{kv,\ell}h_\ell\)the same, sparse layers, per selected token
\(\nu_I = s_I\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal S}h_{I,\ell}\)bytes per cached token of the scan's own cache (Part 3)
Definition 2FLOPs and bytes of a pass

\(F\) denotes FLOPs and \(Q\) bytes, per sequence and per pass, for an AR step and for a TD pass, each split into a linear part and an attention part. A TD pass here is a commit pass, the full network over the \(b\) positions of the canvas; a denoising pass costs \(r\) times as much (A3).

Linear FLOPs

\[ \class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}} = 2N_{\mathrm{act}},\qquad \class{mj-td}{F^{TD}_{\mathrm{lin}}} = 2b\,N_{\mathrm{act}},\qquad N_{\mathrm{act}} = W_{\mathrm{ne}} + L\,k\,W^e. \]

Attention FLOPs

\[ \begin{aligned} \class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) &= \alpha_G C + \alpha_W\min(C,w) + \alpha_S\min(C,m) + \alpha_I C,\\[2pt] \class{mj-td}{F^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) &= b\,\class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C). \end{aligned} \]
\[ \begin{gathered} \class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) = \alpha_G C + \alpha_W\min(C,w)\\ \qquad + \alpha_S\min(C,m) + \alpha_I C,\\[3pt] \class{mj-td}{F^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) = b\,\class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C). \end{gathered} \]

Linear bytes

\[ \class{mj-ar}{W_{AR}}(B) = W_{\mathrm{ne}} + L\,U_{E,k}(B)\,W^e,\qquad \class{mj-td}{W_{TD}}(B) = W_{\mathrm{ne}} + L\,U_{E,k}(Bb)\,W^e. \]
\[ \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(B) = \frac{s_w\class{mj-ar}{W_{AR}}(B)}{B},\qquad \class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(B) = \frac{s_w\class{mj-td}{W_{TD}}(B)}{B}. \]

Attention bytes

\[ \begin{aligned} \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) &= \nu_G C + \nu_W\min(C,w) + \nu_S\min(C,m) + \nu_I C,\\[2pt] \class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) &= \nu_G C + \nu_W\min(C,w) + \nu_S\,U_{C,m}(b) + \nu_I C. \end{aligned} \]
\[ \begin{gathered} \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) = \nu_G C + \nu_W\min(C,w)\\ \qquad + \nu_S\min(C,m) + \nu_I C,\\[3pt] \class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C) = \nu_G C + \nu_W\min(C,w)\\ \qquad + \nu_S\,U_{C,m}(b) + \nu_I C. \end{gathered} \]

The totals are \(F^X = F^X_{\mathrm{lin}} + F^X_{\mathrm{attn}}\) and \(Q^X = Q^X_{\mathrm{lin}} + Q^X_{\mathrm{attn}}\) for \(X \in \{AR, TD\}\).

Intensities and penalties

Whether a pass is memory-bound or compute-bound depends only on its arithmetic intensity, the ratio of its FLOPs to its bytes, compared with the ridge point of the accelerator (Definition 3).

TD is hurt more by sparsity than AR. The following penalties quantify this: on the linear layers, on attention and overall, they compare the bytes that a TD pass and an AR step read per sequence,

\[ \Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}(B) = \frac{\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(B)}{\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(B)} = \frac{\class{mj-td}{W_{TD}}(B)}{\class{mj-ar}{W_{AR}}(B)},\qquad \Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}(C) = \frac{\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C)}{\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(C)},\qquad \Pi(B,C) = \frac{\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}}(B,C)}{\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}}(B,C)}, \]
\[ \begin{gathered} \Pi_{\mathrm{lin}} = \frac{\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{lin}}}}{\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}} = \frac{\class{mj-td}{W_{TD}}}{\class{mj-ar}{W_{AR}}},\\[4pt] \Pi_{\mathrm{attn}} = \frac{\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}}{\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}},\qquad \Pi = \frac{\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}}}{\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}}}, \end{gathered} \]

so that \(\class{mj-td}{I^{TD}_{\mathrm{lin}}} = b\,\class{mj-ar}{I^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}/\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\), \(\class{mj-td}{I^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}} = b\,\class{mj-ar}{I^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}/\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\) and \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = b\,\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}/\Pi\). Moreover, since \(\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}} = \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}} + \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}\), the overall penalty is the average of the two penalties, weighted by the shares \(\class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}} = \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}/\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}}\) and \(\class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}} = \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}/\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}}\) of an AR step's bytes (Proposition 2)

\[ \Pi = \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}\,\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}} + \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}\,\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}. \]

We have that:

  • \(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) relates to the sparsity in Mixture of Experts (MoE).
  • \(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\) relates to the sparsity in sparse attention layers. 4

The throughput gain

In this section, Proposition 1 gives the ratio of the TD and the AR throughput. We then read off which decoder wins in Corollary 1. Finally, Proposition 2 splits each intensity into a linear part and an attention part, which Parts 2 and 3 treat separately.

Proposition 1TD/AR throughput gain
A1 · Roofline
On an accelerator with peak compute \(\pi\) (FLOP/s) and memory bandwidth \(\beta\) (bytes/s), a pass with \(F\) FLOPs and \(Q\) bytes read from memory takes \(\max(F/\pi,\,Q/\beta)\).
A2 · Costs
Per sequence, an AR step costs \(\class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}}\) FLOPs and \(\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}}\) bytes, and a TD pass \(\class{mj-td}{F^{TD}}\) and \(\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}}\), as in Definition 2. Vocabulary, activations, KV writes and in-canvas keys are neglected.
A3 · Canvas
A canvas commits \(b\) tokens per sequence after \(S\) denoising passes and one commit pass. A denoising pass costs \(r\) times a commit pass, in FLOPs and in bytes.
A4 · Lockstep
\(B\) sequences share every pass, at a context \(C\) held fixed over a canvas.
A5 · Routing
Expert routing and token selection are independent across positions and uniform: each token picks its \(k\) experts uniformly among the \(E\), and each query its \(m\) tokens uniformly among the \(C\).5

Then TD's throughput over AR's is

\[ \boxed{\;\begin{gathered}\Gamma = \frac{1}{\omega}\cdot\frac{\min(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}},\,I^\star)}{\min(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}},\,I^\star)},\\[6pt] \omega = S\,r+1,\qquad \class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = \frac{b}{\Pi}\,\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}.\end{gathered}\;} \]
Proof
  1. For a pass with \(I = F/Q\): \(\max(F/\pi,\,Q/\beta) = \dfrac{F}{\beta}\max\Bigl(\dfrac{1}{I^\star},\dfrac{1}{I}\Bigr) = \dfrac{F}{\beta\,\min(I, I^\star)}\).
  2. AR. A step costs \(B\class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}}\) FLOPs at intensity \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}\) and yields \(B\) tokens: \(\class{mj-ar}{T_{AR}} = \class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}}\,/\,\bigl(\beta\min(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}, I^\star)\bigr)\) per token.
  3. TD. A commit pass costs \(B\class{mj-td}{F^{TD}} = Bb\class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}}\) FLOPs at intensity \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}}\). A denoising pass multiplies both \(\class{mj-td}{F^{TD}}\) and \(\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}}\) by \(r\), so it has the same intensity and takes \(r\) times as long. A canvas therefore takes \(\omega\) times one commit pass and yields \(Bb\) tokens: \(\class{mj-td}{T_{TD}} = \omega \class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}}\,/\,\bigl(\beta\min(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}}, I^\star)\bigr)\) per token.
  4. \(\Gamma = \class{mj-ar}{T_{AR}}/\class{mj-td}{T_{TD}}\), and \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = \class{mj-td}{F^{TD}}/\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}} = b\class{mj-ar}{F^{AR}}/(\Pi \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}}) = b\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}/\Pi\) by Definition 4. \(\blacksquare\)

Figure 7 · interactive

The roofline bound \(\Gamma\) depends on the accelerator only through its ridge point.

The curve is the gain for a chip of ridge point \(I^\star = \pi/\beta\); each dot is an accelerator. Drag the marker along the axis, select a dot, or switch to long context.

Exact roofline bounds, DiffusionGemma, BF16, \(b = 256\), \(S = 14\). Multiplying the peak \(\pi\) and the bandwidth \(\beta\) by the same factor divides the time of every pass by the same factor, so \(\Gamma\) depends on the accelerator only through \(I^\star\), and the accelerators lie on the curve. Over this range a higher ridge point never lowers the gain, at short or at long context. Short context: \(C = 1{,}024\), at the batch that maximises \(\Gamma\); on the flat stretch near \(I^\star = 60\), batch 1 is best and both decoders are memory-bound, so the gain is \(\mathrm{TPF}/\Pi\) whatever the ridge. Long context: \(C = 2^{20}\) at batch 1; the dashed line is the limit \(I^\star/(\omega I_{\mathrm{attn}})\) as \(C \to \infty\), linear in \(I^\star\). Over this range the curve lies above the line, because at batch 1 the weights are still about a quarter of an AR step's bytes; above \(I^\star \approx 620\) a TD pass at batch 1 is itself memory-bound at this context, and the curve is flat. The curve assumes unlimited memory; a hollow dot marks an accelerator in which the model and its KV cache do not fit. Both axes are logarithmic.

What the formulas leave out

  • Vocabulary and self-conditioning. With self-conditioning, each denoising pass after the first feeds the token distribution predicted by the previous pass back in through the embedding matrix. Per token, TD therefore runs \(2S-1\) vocabulary-sized matrix multiplications against AR's one, and a cheaper denoising network (\(r < 1\)) does not shrink them. The formulas leave them out, but the maps and the calculator include them.
  • Timing kernel by kernel. Assumption (A1) gives a pass the time of one kernel in which all of its compute and memory traffic overlap. A pass is a chain of kernels, and adding their roofline times, \(\sum_c \max(F_c/\pi, Q_c/\beta)\), with \(F_c\) and \(Q_c\) the FLOPs and bytes of kernel class \(c\), is never faster and at most twice as slow. For an AR step at moderate batch every class is memory-bound and nothing changes. For a TD pass in BF16 (\(s_w = 2\)), the dense layers, of intensity \(2Bb/s_w\), are compute-bound from batch 1, while the experts, of intensity \(2Bbk/(s_wE)\), stay memory-bound until \(Bbk/E \approx I^\star\), batch 13 here; at context 1k on an H200, in the exact accounting, the best batch moves from 5 to 9 and the peak gain from 5.3× to 3.8× (Figure 11). The calculator offers both rules.
  • Small effects. The formulas leave out activations, KV writes, and the at most \(b\) keys inside the canvas6.
  • Keys equal to values on the global layers. DiffusionGemma's global layers project one tensor that serves as both key and value. In this blogpost, we cache it twice (\(\kappa^c = 2\))7. On the other hand, a cache that stored it once would halve the global layers' bytes, double \(I_{\mathrm{attn}}\) to 16 and halve the long-context limit \(I^\star/(\omega I_{\mathrm{attn}})\) (regime R6, Part 4) from 1.72 to 0.86.
  • Cross-layer KV sharing. Sharing one KV cache across layers divides the cache's size, but not the bytes read per pass, since each layer still reads the shared cache. Hence, it changes the largest batch that fits in memory, not any intensity.
  • Beyond the roofline. Finally, the formulas leave out kernel efficiency, uneven and correlated expert routing (which affects \(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\)), adaptive step counts (which affect \(\omega\)) and correlated token selections (which affect \(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\)).

Which side wins

Proposition 1 compares two minima, so which decoder wins depends first on AR: if AR is compute-bound, TD loses, and otherwise the gain is the smaller of \(\mathrm{TPF}/\Pi\), set by the bytes, and \(I^\star/(\omega \class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}})\), set by the compute that AR leaves idle (Corollary 1).

Corollary 1Which side wins

  1. If AR is compute-bound (\(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} \ge I^\star\)), then \(\Gamma \le 1/\omega\), with equality whenever \(\Pi \le b\), since then \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} \ge \class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}\); this holds under (A2) and (A5) by Proposition 3(4). Otherwise

    \[ \Gamma = \min\Bigl(\frac{\mathrm{TPF}}{\Pi},\ \frac{I^\star}{\omega\,\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}}\Bigr),\quad \mathrm{TPF} = \frac{b}{\omega}. \]

    In particular, \(\Gamma \ge 1\) exactly when both \(\mathrm{TPF} \ge \Pi\) and \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} \le I^\star/\omega\): a TD pass must serve more tokens per read than it pays in penalty, and AR must use at most a fraction \(1/\omega\) of the compute, so that TD's \(\omega\) times more FLOPs fit in what AR leaves idle.

  2. Suppose AR is memory-bound. Treat \(B\) as a real variable and assume that \(\Pi(\cdot, C)\) is non-increasing in \(B\). Since \(\class{mj-ar}{W_{AR}}(B)/B\) is non-increasing (proof of Proposition 4), \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}(\cdot, C)\) is non-decreasing in \(B\), and \(\Gamma\) is maximal at the batch \(\class{mj-td}{B^\star_{TD}}(C)\) at which \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = I^\star\), or at \(B = 1\) if \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}}(1, C) \ge I^\star\); if \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}}(\cdot, C) \lt I^\star\) at every batch, \(\Gamma = \mathrm{TPF}/\Pi\) is non-decreasing in \(B\). Over integer batches the maximum is at \(\lfloor \class{mj-td}{B^\star_{TD}}(C)\rfloor\) or \(\lceil \class{mj-td}{B^\star_{TD}}(C)\rceil\). The assumption on \(\Pi\) can fail.8
Proof

(1) If \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} \ge I^\star\) the denominator of Proposition 1 is \(I^\star\) and the numerator at most \(I^\star\), with equality when \(\Pi \le b\), since then \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = b\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}/\Pi \ge \class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} \ge I^\star\). Otherwise \(\min(b\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}/\Pi,\,I^\star)/\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} = \min(b/\Pi,\,I^\star/\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}})\); divide by \(\omega\). A minimum of two numbers is at least 1 exactly when both are. (2) The first term of the minimum is non-decreasing in \(B\) and the second is non-increasing. The minimum of two such functions is maximal where they cross, which is where \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = b\,\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}/\Pi = I^\star\), or at \(B = 1\) if the first is already the larger there. Over integer batches the minimum is non-decreasing up to \(\lfloor \class{mj-td}{B^\star_{TD}}(C)\rfloor\) and non-increasing from \(\lceil \class{mj-td}{B^\star_{TD}}(C)\rceil\) on. \(\blacksquare\)

Corollary 1(1) specialises to the two extremes as follows:

  • Short context: \(\Pi = \Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) and \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} = \class{mj-ar}{I^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(B)\). Hence, the first condition of Corollary 1(1) is a lower bound on the batch (the linear penalty must fall below TPF), and the second is an upper bound (the parity batch \(B_\times\) of Part 2).
  • Long context: \(\Pi = \Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\) and \(\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} = \class{mj-ar}{I^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}\), and neither condition depends on the batch.

For DiffusionGemma on an H200, both conditions hold at every batch up to 109 at short context, and at every batch at long context.9

Linear and attention parts

The bytes of a pass split into the weights, read by the linear layers, and the KV cache, read by attention; each intensity is then the average of its two parts, weighted by these bytes, and lies nearer to the part that carries more of them (Proposition 2).

Proposition 2Each intensity is a byte-weighted average of its linear and attention parts

Under (A2), for \(X \in \{AR, TD\}\), let \(\theta^X_{\mathrm{lin}} = Q^X_{\mathrm{lin}}/Q^X\) and \(\theta^X_{\mathrm{attn}} = Q^X_{\mathrm{attn}}/Q^X\) be the shares of the two parts in the bytes of Definition 2. Then

\[ I_X = \theta^X_{\mathrm{lin}}\,I^X_{\mathrm{lin}} + \theta^X_{\mathrm{attn}}\,I^X_{\mathrm{attn}},\qquad \Pi - 1 = \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}} - 1) + \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}} - 1). \]
\[ \begin{gathered} I_X = \theta^X_{\mathrm{lin}}\,I^X_{\mathrm{lin}} + \theta^X_{\mathrm{attn}}\,I^X_{\mathrm{attn}},\\[4pt] \Pi - 1 = \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{lin}}}(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}} - 1)\\ \qquad + \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_{\mathrm{attn}}}(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}} - 1). \end{gathered} \]

Consequently each intensity lies between its two parts, nearer to the part that carries more of that pass's bytes. Moreover \(1/\Pi = \class{mj-td}{\theta^{TD}_{\mathrm{lin}}}/\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}} + \class{mj-td}{\theta^{TD}_{\mathrm{attn}}}/\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\), so \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}}/\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}} = b/\Pi\) lies between \(b/\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) and \(b/\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\).

Proof

\(I_X = F^X/Q^X = \sum_c (Q^X_c/Q^X)(F^X_c/Q^X_c)\) over the two parts \(c\). For the penalty, \(\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_c} = \Pi_c\,\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_c}\) by Definition 4, so \(\Pi - 1 = \sum_c (\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}_c} - \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_c})/\class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}} = \sum_c \class{mj-ar}{\theta^{AR}_c}(\Pi_c - 1)\). Similarly, \(1/\Pi = \sum_c \class{mj-ar}{Q^{AR}_c}/\class{mj-td}{Q^{TD}} = \sum_c \class{mj-td}{\theta^{TD}_c}/\Pi_c\). A weighted average with non-negative weights lies between its terms; \(\class{mj-td}{I_{TD}} = (b/\Pi)\class{mj-ar}{I_{AR}}\) and \(\Pi\) lies between \(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) and \(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}\). \(\blacksquare\)

Notes

  1. As emphasized in the introduction, we do not consider parallel decoding techniques for AR such as Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) or Speculative Sampling (SS). The Conclusion discusses speculative decoding among related work. ↩
  2. In the case of DiffusionGemma we always have \(r=1\), but one could get creative regarding the encoder-decoder architecture. ↩
  3. There are no sparse attention layers in our running example with DiffusionGemma. However, since recent models such as Qwen 3.8 Flash Next use sparse attention layers and they impact the throughput gains, we include them in our analysis. ↩
  4. In particular, in DiffusionGemma we have \(\Pi_{\mathrm{attn}}=1\). ↩
  5. Part 6 measures the routing: it is not independent, and Remark 2 there gives Proposition 1 at the measured routing. ↩
  6. Activations stay in on-chip memory when consecutive operations are fused into one kernel. ↩
  7. As vLLM does; the global-attention kernel of Part 8 also reads keys and values as two tensors. ↩
  8. For \(b = 8\), \(\Pi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) is 3.52 at batch 1 and 3.70 at batch 2 (Proposition 3). ↩
  9. With dense attention. With the sparse variant of Part 3, the second condition fails at long context, since \(I_{\mathrm{idx}} = 16 \gt I^\star/\omega = 13.7\). ↩
